scenes.dialogue: A State sued in the Supreme Court in nineteen ninety six for its share of power, and won it in twenty eleven. So why was it still waiting for its arrears?
scenes.shown: A State sued in the Supreme Court in 1996 for its share of power, and won it in 2011. So why was it still waiting for its arrears?

scenes.dialogue: The Centre put those arrears at over thirteen thousand million units. But Punjab said Himachal itself owed over six thousand crore rupees in costs. Who owes whom?
scenes.shown: The Centre put those arrears at over 13,000 million units. But Punjab said Himachal itself owed over ₹6,000 crore in costs. Who owes whom?

scenes.dialogue: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On the sixth of November, Honourable Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana ruled.
scenes.shown: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On 6 November, Honourable Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana ruled.

scenes.dialogue: When Punjab was split in nineteen sixty six, part of it went to Himachal. So Himachal claimed a share of the Bhakra Nangal and Beas power.
scenes.shown: When Punjab was split in 1966, part of it went to Himachal. So Himachal claimed a share of the Bhakra-Nangal and Beas power.

scenes.dialogue: It sought seven point one nine percent, its share of Punjab's population. In twenty eleven, the Court granted it, but refused its claim to twelve percent free power.
scenes.shown: It sought 7.19%, its share of Punjab's population. In 2011, the Court granted it, but refused its claim to 12% free power.

scenes.dialogue: The Court asked the Centre to compute the arrears within six months. The Centre's figure came in twenty thirteen, but Punjab and Haryana disputed it.
scenes.shown: The Court asked the Centre to compute the arrears within six months. The Centre's figure came in 2013, but Punjab and Haryana disputed it.

scenes.dialogue: After years of mediation, the Attorney General proposed a cashless settlement. Himachal and Haryana agreed in principle. Punjab objected.

scenes.dialogue: Finally, what did the Supreme Court decide? Punjab's objections were an attempt to reopen what the twenty eleven decree had settled, so they were rejected.

scenes.dialogue: Himachal's share of the capital cost is set off against its arrears, and the rest comes over twenty lean seasons. The Court warned that its directions are binding.
